security_audit.summary: Most static detections are false positives caused by Markdown backticks and documentation examples, not Ruby or shell backtick execution. The confirmed risks are bundled helper commands that write local files, unfiltered recursive packaging, and missing validation for path-like skill names. No prompt injection attempt was found in the reviewed skill files.

remediation.issue: The initializer accepts path-like skill names before creating files.
remediation.suggestion: Validate skill_name against the documented hyphen-case pattern and verify the resolved skill directory remains under the requested base path.

remediation.issue: Recursive packaging may include unintended files or symlink targets.
remediation.suggestion: Exclude hidden files, credentials, caches, VCS directories, generated archives, and symlinks before writing the zip archive.

remediation.issue: SKILL.md instructs agents to run bundled scripts that write local files.
remediation.suggestion: Document expected inputs, output paths, and file effects directly before each command example.

remediation.issue: The packager can write the output archive into a broad or unintended directory.
remediation.suggestion: Require an explicit output directory or warn before writing archives outside a project-controlled dist folder.

semantic_findings.title: Path-Like Skill Names Can Escape the Target Directory
semantic_findings.description: init_skill combines a resolved base path with the caller-supplied skill_name before creating files. Because skill_name is not validated, names containing path separators or traversal segments can create a skill directory outside the intended output folder.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The script uses argv values directly and does not enforce the printed hyphen-case naming rules before building the output path. The impact depends on the caller supplying a path-like skill name.

semantic_findings.title: Unfiltered Recursive Packaging May Include Secrets
semantic_findings.description: package_skill walks every file under the selected skill directory and adds it to the zip archive. Without exclusions for hidden files, credentials, caches, VCS folders, or symlink targets, authors can accidentally publish sensitive local files.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The code directly recurses through the selected skill directory and writes each file to the archive. The exposure depends on files or symlinks present in the folder, so confidence is high but not absolute.

content.value_statement: Building reusable AI skills is hard when structure, metadata, and packaging rules are unclear. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through planning, scaffolding, editing, validation, and packaging.
actual_capabilities: Explains the required SKILL.md structure, YAML metadata, and optional bundled resources.
Guides authors through gathering concrete examples before writing a skill.
Helps choose when to use scripts, references, and assets for reusable work.
Provides an initializer script that creates a template skill directory.
Provides validation and packaging scripts for distributable skill zip files.
limitations: It does not publish skills to a marketplace or remote registry.
It only performs basic validation and does not replace a security audit.
Generated templates still need domain content, testing, and cleanup before release.
Authors must review skill names, paths, and package contents before running helper scripts.

use_cases.title: Create an Internal Automation Skill
use_cases.description: Plan and scaffold a skill that captures repeatable team workflows, helper scripts, and reference documents.

use_cases.title: Document a Team Workflow
use_cases.description: Convert a known process into clear skill instructions with examples, resource choices, and validation steps.

use_cases.title: Prepare a Community Skill Package
use_cases.description: Review structure, remove placeholder files, validate metadata, and package the skill for distribution.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Simple Skill
prompt_templates.prompt: I want to create a skill for [task]. Ask the key questions, then propose a concise SKILL.md outline and needed resources.

prompt_templates.title: Scaffold a New Skill
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the skill-creator workflow to initialize a new skill named [skill-name] in [workspace path], then explain what files I should customize.

prompt_templates.title: Improve an Existing Skill
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my existing skill files for metadata quality, resource organization, missing examples, and leftover template content.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare for Release
prompt_templates.prompt: Evaluate this skill for release readiness. Check validation issues, packaging risks, unnecessary files, and whether the instructions support repeated use.

output_examples.input: Create a skill for turning meeting notes into action plans.
output: Recommended structure: workflow-based skill with intake, extraction, prioritization, and review sections.
Reusable resources: a reference checklist for action item quality and optional templates for final summaries.
Next step: gather two real note samples before finalizing the instructions.
Metadata is specific enough to trigger on the intended task.
The references folder is useful, but one placeholder asset should be removed.
Package only after checking for private files, symlinks, and generated archives.

output_examples.input: Help me decide whether this skill needs a script.
output: A script is useful because the task repeats deterministic file processing steps.
Keep business rules in SKILL.md and put long API details in references.
Document script inputs, outputs, and failure cases before release.

best_practices: Start with real user examples before writing the final skill instructions.
Keep SKILL.md concise and move detailed reference material into references.
Use hyphen-case skill names and inspect package contents before distribution.
anti_patterns: Publishing a skill that still contains TODO placeholders or generic template text.
Bundling large reference files without clear loading guidance or search patterns.
Using path-like skill names or unchecked folders when running helper scripts.

faq.question: What does this skill help create?
faq.answer: It helps create reusable AI skills with clear instructions, metadata, optional resources, validation, and packaging.

faq.question: Can it work with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The marketplace metadata lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Does it generate a complete finished skill automatically?
faq.answer: No. It creates structure and guidance, but authors must add domain content, examples, and tests.

faq.question: Does it include validation?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes a basic validator for frontmatter, naming, description format, and required files.

faq.question: What files can the initializer create?
faq.answer: It can create SKILL.md plus example scripts, references, and assets folders for customization.

faq.question: Should authors remove generated example files?
faq.answer: Yes. Authors should delete unused examples, placeholders, private files, symlinks, and generated archives before packaging.
